title: Put a quantum-advantage claim through an evidence gate
description: Select the workload and benchmark boundary. The gate rewards complete evidence, not an attractive circuit-only timing.

scenarios.label: Quantum kernel on customer vectors
scenarios.detail: Classical features must be encoded before pairwise quantum-kernel measurements.
scenarios.inputEvidence: State preparation is part of the algorithmic cost and must be timed.

scenarios.label: Classify quantum sensor states
scenarios.detail: The inputs already exist as quantum states, so full classical tomography may be avoidable.
scenarios.inputEvidence: Quantum-native data removes one loading objection, but it does not prove a useful advantage.

scenarios.label: QAOA for feature subset search
scenarios.detail: A classical objective is mapped to a constrained combinatorial search problem.
scenarios.inputEvidence: Include objective construction, parameter tuning, and every sampled candidate in wall-clock cost.

boundaries.label: Circuit execution only
boundaries.detail: Excludes data preparation, compilation, queues, tuning, and repeated trials.

boundaries.label: One hardware run
boundaries.detail: Includes compilation and measurements, but not the complete experiment lifecycle.

boundaries.label: End-to-end repeated study
boundaries.detail: Includes inputs, compilation, queueing, tuning, measurements, and repeated trials.

baselines.label: Naive classical baseline
baselines.detail: A convenient default model with little tuning.

baselines.label: Tuned task baseline
baselines.detail: A suitable classical method with a documented search budget.

baselines.label: Best known practical baseline
baselines.detail: A competitive solver or model measured on the same quality target and hardware budget.
